limits: Only declared rates, workers, seeds, and synthetic contracts were tested. Passing thresholds are lower bounds; absent saturation ceilings prevent capacity-ratio proof.
Different valid transaction orders can change useful effects and generation occupancy. Missing/deferred outcomes do not establish lost committed data.
Retry stages do not attribute true overlap versus overly broad predicate conflicts. Global queries can have genuine conflicts.

Query calls include failed attempts. Candidate rows count after completed index lookups but before point reads; returned rows and successful time count only completed queries. Aggregates include transaction attempts that subsequently abort. Ratios therefore describe collected work, not per-committed-message cost or exact false-positive rates.
Initial/final fleet counts are snapshots, not concurrent runtime minima; more than configured identities can reflect simultaneous generations in the two-bank pool.

Native expiry indexing includes every active record event_time while PostgreSQL event_time_idx is partial for active kinds POSITION/OUTBOX/DEDUP. This concrete adapter schema confound calls for a matching narrow native expiry index control before attributing expiry amplification to the engine. Both due indexes are partial; that control alone cannot explain due-query costs or establish retry causes.
Interactive service results combine ownership with per-operation RPC and serialization overhead; these data do not isolate those costs.
Metrics companions establish reproducible same-source/configuration recorded cases, not witnesses for the unrecorded execution.
scope: Independent compact report review. No history is inferred for failed or metrics-only executions; all declared trials are retained.
